chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Jam sessions at Music Town: Nat Cole, Jacquet and Norman Granz
summary: Drama teacher Frances Williams brought Norman Granz to hold Sunday jam sessions at the hall, with players such as Nat Cole, Illinois and Russell Jacquet and Red Callender.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So...then...later, there was music in that building, later, like in the '50s, they started having jam sessions there. You had some jam sessions and things when you operated Music Town.
Yeah, I told you who was up there.
Yeah, but you didn't tell me on the tape, I don't think, did you? I don't think so.
Oh, you know the fellow...oh, what's his name?
Well, you showed me a picture of Nat Cole. Was that where...
Nat Cole used to play up there...and Jacquet and, oh, all of the...
Russell and Illinois, right?
What was the boy that I told you started to running them up there? That it...
Oh, Norman Granz.

SPIKES - 143
Reel 4
Page 37
Norman Granz, yeah.
Tell me about how that started.

Well, he uh...I had a woman that...he was... Norman Granz was havin' 'em around a little here and there in Hollywood and around, and I had a woman up there teachin' drama named...uh... Williams, so she said, "Oh, Reb, why don't you have a jam session over here?" I don't know nothin' about it. I said, "What is it?" And she told me. And she said, "I'll go and talk to Norman Granz," and she went out and talked to him, and he moved over there.
Was that Frances Williams?
Frances Williams. Yeah.
Oh, I know her.
She worked up there with me. Is she still living?
Oh, yes, I think so. I saw her a year or so ago.
Yeah? So, she come over there and was teachin' drama--dramatics.
She's an actress, yes.
And she went out and brought Norman Granz over there, and after that, he used to jam every Sunday.
So what year did Norman start having his sessions there?
Oh, I guess it was...I don't know...'45, '46... something like that, I think it was. I don't know. Maybe it was before that.
It might have been before that because I think

SPIKES - 144
Reel 4
Page 38
he started his Jazz At The Philharmonic...uh...
Oh, this before he started...
That was about '45...
I know the boys that had the Philharmonic Record Shop down there under the Philharmonic.
Who were they?
I can't think of them now. They uh...they lived over here on...near where you said you lived...on...
Edgehill?

Two Jewish boys, and they had the record store down there, and they made a lot of money. They had two or three hit records, and after that, they really went on out for themselves in a record company, I think. And I don't know what year it was now. It might have been during the war when Austin was away. I don't remember now but anyway, he come over there, and he used to have them there every Sunday. He had all the big white musicians and everything over there.
Remember some of the people who played for him?

No. I didn't meddle with his business, you know. I just rented him the hall, and I know Jacquet they would call and King Cole and Red Callender--a few of them, you know, I knew, but a lot of those white boys who had big names--I didn't know them. I knew them when I heard 'em talked about but I didn't know 'em personally or anything.
